Gauged support for a rating

Source: R/accessors.R
rating_support.Rd

How much of each limb rests on gaugings: how many fall inside it, the stage range they cover, and how far the limb extends beyond them at either end. A limb that stretches well past its highest gauging is an extrapolation there, whatever its fit statistics say.

Usage

rating_support(x)

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating or FlodeSegmentedRating. A FlodeRatingTable holds equations only, with no gaugings to measure support against.

Value

A data.table. For a FlodeRating, one row per limb: limb, lower_stage_m, upper_stage_m, n_gaugings, gauged_min_stage_m, gauged_max_stage_m, lower_unsupported_m and upper_unsupported_m (how far the limb extends below its lowest and above its highest gauging, m), and the same as a fraction of the limb's width, lower_unsupported_frac and upper_unsupported_frac. A limb with no gaugings has n_gaugings 0 and NA elsewhere. For a FlodeSegmentedRating, one row with n_gaugings, gauged_min_stage_m and gauged_max_stage_m.

See also

flag_extrapolated_limbs() for the same measures with a tolerance applied; rating_evidence()

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage_m <- seq(0.5, 2.5, by = 0.05)
discharge_cms <- 5 * stage_m^1.6 + rnorm(length(stage_m), sd = 0.02)
fit <- rate_optimise(discharge_cms, stage_m)
rating_support(fit)
#>     limb lower_stage_m upper_stage_m n_gaugings gauged_min_stage_m
#>    <int>         <num>         <num>      <int>              <num>
#> 1:     1           0.5           2.5         41                0.5
#>    gauged_max_stage_m lower_unsupported_m upper_unsupported_m
#>                 <num>               <num>               <num>
#> 1:                2.5                   0                   0
#>    lower_unsupported_frac upper_unsupported_frac
#>                     <num>                  <num>
#> 1:                      0                      0
